question: Can a public copper benchmark be mapped directly into an ABF/FCBGA issuer material-cost signal?

physicalEvidence.source: Nan Ya PCB official ABF roadmap
physicalEvidence.finding: ABF substrate product/process roadmap identifies core/PP, dielectric, solder mask and bumping material families, but does not disclose material cost weights.
ABF is a thermosetting insulating film made from epoxy-resin chemistry, hardener and inorganic microparticle filler.
Fine copper interconnections/plating are formed on ABF dielectric layers; copper/ABF interface is physically real and process-critical.

publicBenchmarkEvidence.sourceClass: Taiwan basic-metals monitoring platform / Fastmarkets-derived benchmark

publicBenchmarkEvidence.benchmark: Taiwan refined copper/copper alloy import unit value
publicBenchmarkEvidence.sourceClass: Taiwan basic-metals monitoring platform / customs statistics

coreFalsification: LME copper price is not the same economic object as a substrate maker's realized copper-foil/electroplating procurement cost.
Physical material relevance does not establish cost weight.
ABF dielectric material and copper are separate material families; one commodity benchmark cannot proxy the whole substrate input basket.
A copper rally can coincide with demand strength, FX changes, inventory timing or cost pressure; no permanent stock sign is allowed.
Without issuer selling-price/margin response and product mix, copper movement cannot be called pricing-power evidence.
safeResearchUse: Store copper benchmark as an external input-cost context descriptor only.
Join to issuer/product exposure only as PARTIAL until procurement basis/cost-share evidence exists.
Use future company margin/ASP/volume evidence on native knownAt clocks; never synthesize gross margin from commodity spreads.
